messages.content: You are an expert space systems engineer providing detailed technical specifications.

You are an expert space systems engineer for Project Dyson, a non-profit
planning the construction of a Dyson swarm.

Provide a DETAILED technical proposal for: **Water Pilot (C-type target only)**
Context: Phase 0 - Space Resource Processing

## Phase 0 after the 2026 re-assessment (binding context)

The original Phase 0 plan (a central 50 kt/yr processing station at Sun–Earth L4/L5, crew visits,
production LOX/LH₂, 100 kW-class freighters) was found not to close and is abandoned. Design for the
revised architecture below. Do not re-propose the abandoned design.

### Agreed by all three re-assessment models
- Split Phase 0 into 0A (research + pathfinders) and gated 0B (industrial): Structure agreed; budgets → §3 (All three)
- Abandon 50 kt/yr central SEL4/L5 ore processing: — (All three)
- Co-locate at least beneficiation and primary processing at the target NEA; ship product, not ore: Reference architecture (All three. GPT: "favoured but not universally optimal". Claude retains a central station fed with ≥20:1 concentrate as an alternative. Gemini's own weighted QOC scores SEL1 marginally higher (see §6).)
- Narrow product to native/reduced Fe-Ni; defer solar-grade Si and oxide-derived Al/Si: Fe-Ni baseline; Al/Si pilot or deferred (All three)
- Delivered product scale of order 1 kt/yr: 0.6–2.5 kt/yr (Claude 0.6–2.2 (central 1.3); Gemini 1.0–2.5 (1.5, of which 0.3 is water); GPT 0.6–1.0 contracted (0.67–1.33 capacity))
- MW-class cargo tugs: 1.0–2.5 MWe each; 10–18 tugs; 150–300 t payload (→ §3 for point values)
- Robots powered by HV tether from site power, with onboard battery for mobility and safe-mode: 1–3 kV; battery 10–50 kWh (Claude 2–3 kV, 10–30 kWh; Gemini 1–3 kV, 15–25 kWh; GPT 20–50 kWh, voltage unspecified)
- Delete the 200–500 MWh Li-ion line; size storage per site: 0.5–15 MWh total (Claude 0.5–3 MWh + thermal; GPT 1.3–3.3 MWh; Gemini <15 MWh (YAML 10 MWh))
- Reject $5/W array pricing: Hardware ~$30–150/W, launch separately accounted (Claude $30–150/W hardware ($50–230 installed incl. launch); Gemini $60–100/W (spec $75, range $50–110); GPT $30–100/W allowance ($45–220 with delivery))
- Replace 32–50 × 100 kg monoprop prospectors: Remote survey + 4–10 EP rendezvous scouts of 200–600 kg (All three agree a monoprop bus has ~0.5–0.8 km/s Δv. Remote-survey method differs (→ §3).)
- Add an Earth-to-space launch/delivery line: Line agreed; magnitude → §3 (All three)
- Add a comms, ground segment and mission-operations line; DSN not assumed free: Line agreed (All three. Claude and GPT reject the round-1 2.5 TB/day (~230 Mbps) figure.)
- Phase 0 uncrewed; remove habitat and quarterly visits: 0 crew visits (All three. Claude and GPT reject the "human-rating" label in favour of structural reserve plus docking/servicing interfaces. Gemini keeps docking ports and structural margins without commenting on the label.)
- Add an EP propellant supply line; xenon not baselined: Line agreed; demand → §3 (All three)
- No production LOX/LH₂ in Phase 0: — (All three. Claude and GPT remove the EML1 depot; Gemini "defers" cryo depots to 0B/Phase 1.)
- Add NRE, pathfinder, spares and contingency lines: Lines agreed; values → §3 (All three)
- Write a full organization (bom-0-7) specification: ~$100–350M (Claude $100–300M; Gemini $150–250M (text $200M); GPT $150–350M)
- Add a debris/contamination requirement and budget tighter than 99%: $50–300M (Threshold → §3)
- Freeze one configuration-controlled baseline; mark legacy documents superseded: — (All three)
- Earth-supplied material as a fallback if microgravity metallurgy fails: — (All three. Ranking relative to lunar → §3.)
- Tie Phase 0 output to Phase 1 demand with a material/purity/date specification: — (All three)
- Add waste-heat rejection (radiators) explicitly: Item agreed; sizing → §3 (All three)

### Owner decisions
- D-01 (accepted 2026-10-12): Fund 0A. Hold 0B as a gated real option, sized at the gate by signed Phase 1 demand. Call Phase 0 a capability programme, not a cost saving.
- D-02 (accepted 2026-10-12): Hybrid: NASA life-cycle gates with TRL/AD² for each critical technology, plus four discriminating gates (target, demand, economics, licence). Stringency follows reversibility.
- D-03 (proposed; treat as interim): Set an ALARP requirement with an interim design ceiling. The number itself goes to modelling, tests and the licensing state.
- D-04 (proposed; treat as interim): Use SEL1 as the reference case. Re-decide jointly with Phase 1 at the 0B gate.
- D-05 (proposed; treat as interim): Select no propellant yet. Cost iodine as the reference case and argon as the alternate, pending the supply audit and life tests. Water EP stays a desk study until a C-type target is confirmed.

Under D-02, KDP-0B (the one-way commitment to 0B production) needs every project-ending technology
at TRL 6 in a relevant environment with no waivers; internal 0A milestones need TRL 4–5.

### This item: bom-0-6 Water Pilot (C-type target only) (0B (conditional))
Accepted scope: A water-extraction pilot, flown only if the selected target is C-type (D-05, proposed). No production LOX/LH₂ and no EML1 depot in Phase 0.

Round-2 proposals for this item (per model; not approved as numbers):
- resize · bom-0-6 ISPP → water pilot · supported by all · quantity: Claude 1 × 10–100 t/yr (C-type conditional); Gemini 2 units, 1,500 t/yr; GPT 1 × 10–30 t/yr · cost: Claude $150–400M; Gemini $250–450M; GPT $100–300M · confidence: low (Claude, GPT); high (Gemini)
- remove · production LOX/LH₂ and EML1 depot · supported by Claude, GPT (Gemini defers) · quantity: 0 · cost: — · confidence: high (GPT)

Critical technologies (TRL re-baseline, panel envelope):
- T13 Asteroid water extraction pilot: TRL 2–4 now, target 6, AD² 5–6, architecture-change

Other Phase 0 items (do not duplicate their scope): bom-0-1 Prospecting Survey and Rendezvous Scouts; bom-0-2 Mining Robots; bom-0-3 Processing Plant at the Target NEA; bom-0-4 MW-class Cargo Tugs; bom-0-5 Site Power, Arrays and Storage; bom-0-7 Organizational Infrastructure; bom-0-8 Earth-to-Space Launch and Delivery; bom-0-9 Communications and Ground Segment; bom-0-10 Mission Operations; bom-0-11 NRE, Ground R&D and Qualification; bom-0-12 0A Pathfinder Demonstrator; bom-0-13 Phase 1 Receiving Node (SEL1); bom-0-14 Spares and Replacements; bom-0-15 Debris and Contamination Control; bom-0-16 Electric-Propulsion Propellant Supply; bom-0-17 Contingency and Reserve.

State quantities and costs as ranges with their basis, split 0A and 0B where the item spans both,
and say where you disagree with the round-2 figures and why.

### Round-2 reconciliation for this item

# Reconciliation: bom-0-6 In-Situ Propellant Production Systems (Phase 0, Round 2)

**Panel:** Claude Opus 5.5 ("Claude"), Gemini 3.8 Flash ("Gemini"), GPT-6.1 Sol ("GPT")
**Rapporteur role:** This document consolidates, attributes and preserves disagreement. It decides nothing. All BOM changes are proposals for human review.

---

## 1. Verdict matrix

| Finding | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0-F11**: Tug propellant not in BOM; ISPP output has no Phase 0 consumer | agree | agree | partly |
| **P0-F15**: Concluded deliberations not written back into specs | partly | agree | partly |
| **P0-F16**: Consensus documents disagree with the BOM | agree | agree | agree |

**Where the panel stands**

- **P0-F11:** All three agree on two points:
  - The current Kr/I tugs cannot consume ISPP products.
  - Tug propellant supply is unbudgeted.

  They disagree on the size of the demand and on whether water EP remains a live closure path. GPT's "partly" rests on its view that annual demand cannot be established from fleet count and per-trip allowances.
- **P0-F15:** All three agree that rq-0-14, rq-0-30, rq-0-47 and rq-0-48 are not reflected in the ISPP specification. The verdicts diverge for two reasons:
  - Claude and GPT cannot verify the "eight of nine" count from the material supplied.
  - Claude and GPT hold that several deliberation numbers must be corrected before write-back. Gemini adopts most of the deliberations as stated, though it also rejects the 700 W cryocooler figure.
- **P0-F16:** Unanimous agreement that the BOM line, the consensus and rq-0-14 describe incompatible architectures. The models differ on what should govern once the documents are reconciled.

---

## 2. Agreed changes

These are specification changes that all three models support, at least in direction. Where the values differ, the consolidated figure is the envelope of the panel's ranges, with each model's range shown.

| Parameter | Old | Consolidated new value / range | Per-model values | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Site / architecture** | Lunar south pole + EML1 (consensus); NEA surface bucket-wheel (BOM) | Integrated with bom-0-3 at L4/L5 | Claude: L4/L5, system TBD. Gemini: Sun–Earth L4/L5. GPT: Lagrange system unresolved. | Which L4/L5 system is chosen is a preserved divergence (§3.1). |
| **Extraction temperature** | Universal 1,000 °C | Reject the universal 1,000 °C. Use staged, feedstock-specific processing, envelope **150–800 °C**. | Claude: staged 150–400 and 400–750 °C. Gemini: 550 °C nominal (400–750), stepped 150/500 °C. GPT: feedstock-specific qualification envelope 300–800 °C. | All three cite Garenne et al. 2014 and King et al. 2015. |
| **Feedstock heating energy** | Unspecified | **0.15–0.45 kWhₜₕ/kg ore** | Claude: 0.15–0.3. Gemini: 0.22 (0.15–0.35). GPT: 0.15–0.45, including process losses. | Claude and GPT place heating in bom-0-3, counted once. Gemini does not state the allocation. |
| **PEM electrolysis specific energy** | 4–8 kWh/kg H₂O | **5.2–7.0 kWhₑ/kg H₂O** (all three ranges overlap at 5.6–6.5) | Claude: 5.5–7.0. Gemini: 5.2–6.5 (5.8 nominal). GPT: 5.6–6.7. | Claude: thermoneutral limit 4.41 kWh/kg. GPT: derived from DOE PEM data at 50–60 kWh/kg H₂. |
| **20 K cryocooler power for 15–40 W heat leak** | 700 W per tank (rq-0-30) | **About 1–11 kWₑ.** The 700 W figure is rejected by all three. | Claude: 1–5.6 kWₑ (10–20% Carnot, 300 K). Gemini: 2.68 kWₑ for 35 W (15% Carnot, 250 K), range 1.8–4.5. GPT: 1–11 kWₑ (5–20% Carnot). | All three state that 700 W implies roughly 30–80% of Carnot, or more than 55%. |
| **ISPP → tug chemical propellant flow (Phase 0)** | Implied | **0 t/yr LOX/LH₂** | All three | Water flow to tugs is a divergence (§3.2). |
| **Item cost** | $2.0B (4 × $500M) | Reduce substantially. Envelope about **$0.35–1.4B**, structured differently by each model. | Claude: $0.35–0.8B committed + $0–0.5B conditional. Gemini: $0.6B ($0.45–0.8B). GPT: $0.3–0.6B development + $0.2–0.8B conditional hardware and integration. | The structure is a divergence (§3.6). |
| **Phasing** | Monolithic Phase 0 deployment | Capture and interface reservation first; conversion deferred and gated. | All three | The gate criteria and whether a pilot flies in 0A are divergences (§3.5, §3.6). |
| **Gas cleanup / purification before electrolysis** | Absent | Required | Claude: inside bom-0-6. Gemini: separate skid (5 t, about $120M NRE). GPT: listed as missing scope. | Location and costing differ (§4). |

**Supported by two models, with the third silent or internally inconsistent**

- **Excavation removed from bom-0-6.** Explicit in Claude and GPT. Implicit in Gemini, which feeds the plant from smelter off-gas.
- **LH₂ liquefaction deferred to Phase 1.** Explicit in Claude and GPT. Gemini defers LH₂ in its Decision 2, but its revised-spec table still carries LH₂ ZBO cooling (2.8 kWₑ), a 35 m sunshield and a 56 t LH₂ yield (see Reviewer note).
- **Electrolysis chain energy, water to LOX + GH₂, excluding heating and LH₂.** Claude: 7–11 kWhₑ/kg. GPT: 6–10 kWhₑ/kg. Gemini gives no chain figure.
- **Water processed per 500 kWe.** Claude: 300–650 t/yr. GPT: 350–580 t/yr at 80% availability. Gemini: 500 t/yr at about 450 kWe including auxiliaries. All three are broadly consistent.
- **Electrolysis product split of 8:1 O:H by mass.** Claude and GPT state it. Both say rq-0-30's 100 t LH₂ + 600 t LOX is a 6:1 engine mixture ratio, not an electrolysis inventory. Gemini does not address this.

---

## 3. Preserved divergences

### 3.1 Which L4/L5 system

| Position | Held by | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Sun–Earth L4/L5, high confidence | Gemini | Stated as fixed under rq-0-14. |
| Unresolved | Claude | The choice moves Earth-delivery cost, and so ISPP value, by about 2–5×. Claude names this as the weakest (information) link in D1. |
| Unresolved | GPT | Sun–Earth and Earth–Moon L4/L5 cannot share one communications, logistics or environmental specification. |

### 3.2 Tug propellant demand and the role of water EP (P0-F11)

**Demand estimate**

| Model | Method | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Power-limited: 2ηP/vₑ² at Isp 1,800 s, η 0.6, 0.5–1.5 MWe per tug, 60–90% duty | 100–130 t per MWe-yr. Fleet uses **0.6–2.4 kt/yr** (central about 1.3 kt/yr). |
| Gemini | Rocket equation per trip: 200 t, 4 km/s round trip, 1 trip per 1.5–2 years per tug | About 51 t per trip. Fleet uses **380–510 t/yr**. |
| GPT | Both methods, illustrative only | If 25 kt/yr crosses a 3–6 km/s loaded leg, at least **4,600–10,100 t/yr**. At 0.4 MW per tug, 15 tugs process only **610–790 t/yr**. GPT says demand is "not established" until a trajectory-and-power model exists. |

**Water EP**

| Position | Held by | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Cannot close | Claude | At about 330 t/MWe-yr, water EP burns 0.6–1.5 t of water per tonne of payload, while ore holds 0.05–0.2 t/t. Claude calls Round 1's water-EP closure "circular": it assumed station water from 25 kt/yr of ore that the fleet cannot move. |
| Live alternative ("Camp B") | Gemini | Removes Earth logistics and closes the bom-0-6 business case. Downsides: Isp 800–1,200 s, erosion, low TRL at multi-hundred-kW scale. bom-0-4 should settle on either iodine or water EP. |
| Not a closure; carry as an alternative pending evidence | GPT | Do not switch propulsion "merely to give ISPP a customer." Carry iodine and water as explicit alternatives until trajectory, endurance and supply evidence closes. |

**Baseline propellant**

- Claude: baseline Earth-supplied iodine.
- Gemini: choose iodine or water EP.
- GPT: carry both as alternatives, and add a separately budgeted Kr/I supply line.

### 3.3 Propellant supply figures

| Quantity | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iodine world output | about 30–33 kt/yr (USGS) | about 35–40 kt/yr (USGS 2024) | about 30–35 kt/yr (USGS MCS 2025) |
| Fleet share of iodine | 2–8% (feasible); 20–50% at gate scale (not credible) | about 1.3% | about 3% at 1 kt/yr; 15–33% at 5–10 kt/yr. GPT says Round 1's "1–5%" does not survive the higher-throughput case. |
| Krypton world output | 0.3–0.7 kt/yr, own estimate, **low confidence** (scaled from xenon) | 300–600 t/yr | **Rejects** the unsourced 300–600 t/yr as a procurement basis. Gives only an atmospheric lower-bound check of about 300 Mt of air per kt of Kr. |
| Krypton verdict | Fails: 2–4× world output | Fails: 80–160% of world output | Unverified at the required scale |
| Iodine delivered to L4/L5 | $1,000–5,000/kg, giving **$0.6–12B/yr** | $10,000–20,000/kg, giving **$5–10B/yr** | Not quantified |

Separately, Claude judges rq-0-14's $10–20k/kg Earth-supplied propellant cost as a "plausible upper range" within its wider $1–20k/kg band.

### 3.4 Correcting the deliberations (P0-F15)

| Item | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
|---|---|---|---|
| rq-0-14: 70–90 t/yr at 500 kW | Matches the **H₂ mass**; wrong by 4–8× as a propellant figure | Not challenged | Implies 39–50 kWh/kg, or large unreported downtime; "not an electrolysis-only result" |
| rq-0-30: 190-day subcooling margin | **Holds (conservative).** About 4.0 GJ stored; 3.2 years at 40 W; 190 days corresponds to about 240 W. Flags pressurant need near the triple point. | Adopted as stated | **Does not confirm it is conservative.** 2.5–5 GJ; 210–1,450 days at 40–135 W; 190 days corresponds to about 150–300 W. Needs H₂ property data, pressure limits, stratification and ortho/para treatment. |
| rq-0-47 (40–135 W) vs rq-0-30 (15–40 W) | The higher figure **governs**, giving 3–19 kWₑ at the 20 K stage | Uses 35 W | They are **not competing measurements** of one tank. Different inventory and geometry, so the larger cannot simply be chosen. 3–38 kWₑ at 40–135 W. |
| rq-0-48: MLI degradation 2–3.5× and LBMLI preference | Reasonable judgement; treat as a hypothesis | Adopted, with 3× cooler margin and 4× power margin | Unvalidated design hypotheses; use as test cases |
| rq-0-11, rq-0-18, rq-0-28, rq-0-29 | Not supplied; cannot verify | Not discussed | Gives dispositions for each (e.g. no automatic ISPP mass for human-rating; no ISPP hardware allowance for governance), but notes full conclusions for rq-0-28 and rq-0-29 were not supplied |
| Station spin | Not addressed | Non-spinning station with capillary PMDs; possible local centrifuge for phase separation | No whole-station spin required, but local acceleration is not prohibited. These are separate decisions. |

GPT adds four corrections that no other model raised:

- Smelter waste heat is an added tank heat load, not a cold sink.
- Subcooling does not reduce steady-state heat leak.
- 100 t of LH₂ occupies about 1,400 m³, a sphere roughly 14 m across.
- Insolation on a 100 t tank is about 204 kW before absorptance.

### 3.5 Phase 0B activation gate

| Position | Held by | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Retain ≥25 kt/yr ore throughput and enforce it | Gemini | Do not deploy sunk capital before feedstock delivery is validated. Gemini names "commitment" against political pressure as the weakest link. |
| Replace with measured yield ≥200 t/yr **and** committed demand ≥200 t/yr **and** ≥0.5 MWe power margin | Claude | The fleet delivers only 2–7 kt/yr of ore, so 25 kt/yr is "very likely (~85%)" unreachable. As written, the gate "silently cancels ISPP." |
| Keep 25 kt/yr as a milestone, but it is neither necessary nor sufficient. Require measured yield, contracted demand, power and thermal margins, qualified transfer and storage, and lifecycle economics. | GPT | A small demonstration does not need 25 kt/yr. Commercial production needs more than throughput. |

### 3.6 Quantity, phasing of the first unit, and cost structure

| Model | Phase 0A | Phase 0B | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | **1 pilot (50–150 kWe)**, 3–8 t | 0–2 conditional 0.5 MWe modules, 8–15 t each | $0.35–0.8B committed + $0–0.5B conditional. Real-options justification: the pilot is worth its cost if Phase 1 demand has ≥30% probability (judgement). |
| Gemini | Interface reservation and volatile trap (about $100M) | 1 plant, 12 t (8–16), 450 kWe, 500 t/yr H₂O. F16 text also mentions a flight spare or ground qualification unit. | $0.6B total ($0.45–0.8B); separate prepurification skid $80–150M |
| GPT | **0 production skids** | 1 skid initially, second conditional; 5–15 t per skid; 100–300 t/yr; 0.1–0.5 MWₑ | $0.3–0.6B development + $0.2–0.8B conditional; capture $0.1–0.3B in bom-0-3, counted once. Committed phase total $14.11–14.61B; not a closed budget. |

Claude also notes a reasonable counter-position: capture-and-store only in Phase 0, with zero electrolysis. That is broadly Gemini's and GPT's Phase 0A position.

### 3.7 Water inventory

| Position | Held by | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| 100–1,000 t (nominal 300 t) | Claude | Storage for capture and stockpile |
| 30–100 t working inventory, with a disposition policy | GPT | At 625–4,500 t/yr recovery, 30–100 t fills in about 2–58 days. Full Phase 0A stockpiling "is not automatically justified" and may become a larger project than conversion. |
| Bladder tanks, size unspecified | Gemini | Simple storage at about 280 K |

### 3.8 Delivered product cost

| Position | Held by | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| $200–2,000/kg at the station. Central case $130–330/kg at full utilisation. | Claude | Claude partly disagrees with Round 1: the cost closes if the plant runs fully. The missing piece is a customer, not a cost pathway. |
| Not established | GPT | Capital-only $170–1,400/kg; the low end "is not a delivered-cost forecast." |
| Not addressed | Gemini | — |

### 3.9 Sunshield and product mix

| Model | Product mix | Sunshield |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Water first; LOX only with a committed consumer | None for water; 10–20 m if LOX is stored; 60 m only with LH₂ in Phase 1 |
| Gemini | Water storage (Option B) with provision for on-demand LOX plus 350 bar GH₂ (Option C) | 35 m (25–45 m) modular 12-gore design |
| GPT | Water / LOX + managed GH₂ / LOX-LH₂ all uncommitted | Derive size from actual inventory and geometry; do not buy the 60 m shield now |

### 3.10 Interface values that depend on the throughput assumption

| Interface | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volatile feed from bom-0-3 | 75–900 t/yr (fleet-limited; central about 300) | 500–1,500 t/yr | 625–4,500 t/yr (at 25 kt/yr ore) |
| Process heat | 0.1–0.5 MWₜₕ | Waste-heat rejection 350–500 kWₜₕ (a different flow) | 0.54–1.61 MWₜₕ |
| H₂ disposition | 1–20 t/yr H₂ make-up for a reductant loop in bom-0-3 | 50–100 t/yr GH₂ handling needed | 11–33 t/yr at pilot scale |
| bom-0-5 power conflict (100 MW vs 1–2.5 MW) | Conflicts. $5/W is 20–100× below present space PV cost; one figure must change. | "Shared 100 MW array / 2.5–5 MW bus" | Not necessarily contradictory (phase total vs initial allocation), but unreconciled |
| Data | 0.1–1 Mbps | 2 Mbps | 0.1–1 Mbps average |

### 3.11 What governs once documents are reconciled (P0-F16)

- **Claude:**
  - rq-0-14, as corrected, governs architecture.
  - The BOM governs quantity and budget.
  - Model provenance is metadata only.
  - Regenerate the consensus from the revised spec.
- **GPT:** proposes a hierarchy, highest first:
  1. configuration-controlled requirements;
  2. item specifications and change records;
  3. the BOM;
  4. model syntheses.

  The BOM records the existing estimate but is not proof that its technical description is correct. GPT would regenerate related consensuses only after their source specifications are reconciled. Neither a model consensus nor an uncorrected deliberation governs automatically.
- **Gemini:** rewrites the line item directly to one station plant at Sun–Earth L4/L5, operating at 450–700 °C, for $400–600M.

### 3.12 Fleet power and the 25 kt/yr gate

- **Claude** (only): the 15-tug fleet at about 1 MW per tug delivers 2–7 kt/yr of ore. Meeting 25 kt/yr would need about 60–150 MWe of tug power and 6–15 kt/yr of iodine. Claude also lists 7.5–22 MWe of fleet power with no assigned source.
- **GPT** independently reaches a similar power constraint (610–790 t/yr of propellant processed at 0.4 MW per tug).
- **Gemini** does not address fleet power.

---

## 4. Proposed BOM delta (for human review, not adopted)

| # | Action | Item | Supported by | Quantity | Unit-cost range (USD) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Resize** | bom-0-6, from 4 × $500M to reduced scope | All three (structure differs) | Claude: 1 pilot (50–150 kWe) with gas purification. Gemini: 1 station-integrated plant. GPT: see #2–#4. | Claude: 350M–800M. Gemini: 350M–650M. | Low (Claude, GPT); Medium (Gemini) |
| 2 | **Split** | bom-0-6 development and qualification programme, separate from hardware | GPT (Claude's committed/conditional split is similar in intent) | 1 | 300M–600M | Low |
| 3 | **Add / resize** | Conditional Phase 0B production modules or skids | Claude (0–2 modules of 0.5 MWe); GPT (1–2 skids) | Claude 0–2; GPT 1–2 | 100M–250M each (both) | Low |
| 4 | **Add** | Conditional pilot integration and commissioning | GPT | 1 | 100M–300M | Low |
| 5 | **Add / keep** | Volatile capture and bulk water storage, booked once in bom-0-3 | Claude (add); GPT (keep, add only if not already in the $10B station estimate); Gemini (a Phase 0A reservation of about $100M, carried inside bom-0-6) | 1 | 100M–300M (Claude, GPT); about 100M (Gemini) | Low |
| 6 | **Add** | Volatile prepurification / gas-cleanup skid | Gemini (separate item); Claude (included in #1); GPT (missing scope, uncosted) | 1 | 80M–150M (Gemini) | Medium (Gemini) |
| 7 | **Add (recurring)** | Tug propellant supply and logistics | Claude (costed); Gemini (in text: $5–10B/yr); GPT (separately budgeted Kr/I procurement, storage, loading, delivery; uncosted) | Claude 0.6–2.4 kt/yr; Gemini 380–510 t/yr; GPT pending a trajectory model | Claude: 0.6B–12B per year. Gemini: 5B–10B per year. | Medium (Claude, quantity); Low (cost) |
| 8 | **Remove** | Phase 0 LH₂ liquefaction, cryogenic tank farm, 60 m sunshield | Claude (remove); GPT ("do not purchase now"); Gemini (defers LH₂ in Decision 2 but keeps a 35 m shield and ZBO in its spec) | 0 | 0 | Medium |
| 9 | **Remove** | Integral bucket-wheel excavation from bom-0-6 | GPT (bom_delta); Claude (spec: excavation "None") | 1 scope element | 0 | High (Claude spec) |
| 10 | **Add** | Tug propulsion qualification line (iodine and/or water EP) | GPT (Decision B consequence) | — | Not costed | — |
| 11 | **Add** | Flight spare / ground qualification unit | Gemini (F16 text only) | 1 | Not separately costed | — |

Claude and GPT both caution that capture scope must not be double-counted across bom-0-3 and bom-0-6. GPT also states that the resulting phase total is not a closed budget, because propellant delivery, bulk storage, deployment and servicing remain incompletely costed.

---

## 5. Open questions: what would settle them

# bom-0-6 Water Pilot (C-type Target Only): Technical Proposal

**Phase:** 0B (conditional), with a small 0A sub-line
**Critical technology:** T13 Asteroid water extraction pilot. TRL 2–4 now, target 6, AD² 5–6, architecture-change.
**Status:** Proposal for human review. It supersedes the bom-0-6 "In-Situ Propellant Production Systems" line and all L4/L5 ISPP framings.

---

## 0. Position summary

| Decision | My position | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| What the item is | A water capture, purification and storage pilot integrated with bom-0-3 at the target NEA. It is flown only if the target is C-complex and hydrated. | D-05; revised architecture (ship product, not ore; no central station) |
| What it is not | No LOX/LH₂, no cryogenic storage, no sunshield, no production electrolysis, no EML1 depot, no tug propellant supply. | Agreed by all three; D-05 |
| Quantity | **1 pilot unit.** Two canister-retorts in one skid. | Information purchase, not production |
| Output | **10–30 t/yr water**, design point 25 t/yr at 4 wt% recoverable water. Stretch up to about 50 t/yr if ore exceeds 6 wt%. | Sized by the TRL-6/7 evidence need and site consumables, not by tug demand |
| Ore handled | 600–1,000 t/yr side-stream from bom-0-3 crushing (≤2 mm) | §6 |
| Mass | **7–11 t** launched (point estimate 9.5 t with 25% margin) | §7 bottom-up |
| Power | **55–100 kWₑ** peak, about 65 kWₑ average while operating | §7 |
| Cost, 0A sub-line | **$15–38M**, unconditional (desk study, feedstock characterisation, TRL-5 breadboard) | §12 |
| Cost, 0B | **$135–315M**, spent only if G-W0 confirms a C-type target | §12 |
| Probability-weighted 0B | About $27–126M at P(C-type) = 20–40% | Judgement; see §2.3 |
| Scale-up option W-2 | Full-stream capture kit on bom-0-3's dewatering front-end, 100–300 t/yr, $60–150M. **Not baselined.** Needs a signed consumer. | §5.4 |

**Disagreements with Round 2 (detail in §14)**
- **Gemini (2 units, 1,500 t/yr, high confidence): rejected.** That output needs about 37 kt/yr of ore and roughly 1.3 MWₜₕ of heating. This exceeds the entire site's process scale, and nothing in Phase 0 would consume it.
- **Claude (10–100 t/yr): upper end rejected.**
- **GPT (10–30 t/yr, $100–300M): closest to my view.** My floor is higher because a sulfidation-qualified EDU is unavoidable.

**The key insight that changes how this item should be framed**
If the target is C-type, water handling is not optional. bom-0-3 must dewater all of its ore before or during reducing Fe-oxides. At about 7 kt/yr of ore and 4 wt% water, that liberates around 280 t/yr of water whether anyone wants it or not. So the real choice is between capturing it and venting it under the bom-0-15 contamination budget.

The pilot is therefore three things:
1. The T13 evidence package.
2. The pathfinder for bom-0-3's mandatory dewatering front-end in the C-type branch.
3. The data source for any later decision on water as a product, a reductant make-up or EP propellant.

---

## 1. Design philosophy

1. **Buy information, not tonnes.** The pilot's job is to move T13 to TRL 6 (ground EDU) and then TRL 7 (on site) at representative granular, thermal, chemical and microgravity conditions. Production rate is a by-product.
2. **Keep the hot zone free of solids-handling seals.** The most likely failure in asteroid volatile extraction is abrasive dust at 600 °C in a sealed valve or rotary seal. I remove that failure mode by design: ore is loaded cold into sealed canisters, and only the canister is heated.
3. **Gravity independence by construction.** Spun canisters produce about 0.4 g at the wall. This gives packed-bed wall contact for heat transfer and centrifugal dust rejection from the vapour stream. There is no reliance on free-flowing regolith.
4. **Freeze, don't condense.** Water is captured as frost by vapour deposition on cold fins, then melted in batch in a closed volume. This avoids two-phase gas–liquid separation in microgravity.
5. **Specify performance and contaminant limits, not one temperature.** Following GPT Decision D, temperature is a controlled variable inside a qualified 150–800 °C envelope. The nominal staged profile caps at 650 °C.
6. **Count every flow once.** Pilot retort heating is booked in bom-0-6, because the pilot owns its retorts. Heating for any full-stream dewatering (option W-2) stays in bom-0-3.
7. **Stringency follows reversibility (D-02).** The 0A spend is cheap and reversible. Spending on 0B hardware requires the target gate.

---

## 2. Why the pilot exists, and when it flies

### 2.1 The C-type branch and the Fe-Ni baseline

C-complex targets are poor native-metal sources:
- CI chondrites have essentially no free metal.
- CM chondrites have under about 1% free metal.
- CR chondrites carry several percent Fe-Ni metal in a hydrated matrix.

A C-type selection therefore means one of two things. Either bom-0-3 produces reduced Fe-Ni from magnetite and sulfides, or the target is a CR-like, metal-bearing, hydrated body. Either way bom-0-3 needs a dewatering front-end, and may need H₂ reductant make-up or a carbothermal route using indigenous carbon (CI carries about 3–4 wt% C).

The pilot serves both. It provides make-up water to a bom-0-3 H₂ loop, which bom-0-3 itself electrolyses. It also provides the design data for a dewatering front-end.

### 2.2 Consumers, in priority order

| # | Consumer | Need | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T13 qualification evidence (KDP-0B, Phase 1 decisions) | Yield vs temperature, contaminants, seal and trap life | Certain if the pilot flies |
| 2 | bom-0-3 reductant-loop make-up and thermal-loop fill | 1–20 t/yr H₂O-equivalent (Claude's 1–20 t/yr H₂ make-up is an upper bound in a loop-dominated design) | Depends on bom-0-3 process choice |
| 3 | Water-EP truth data (bom-0-4 / bom-0-16 desk study, D-05) | Real impurity spectrum for thruster tests; 0.1–1 t returned to SEL1 if requested | Desk study only |
| 4 | Phase 1 offtake at SEL1 (bom-0-13) | Unknown | No signed demand |
| — | Tug propellant | Not a consumer | Water EP at 1–2.5 MWₑ × 10–18 tugs needs 3–15 kt/yr, which is 100–500× the pilot (§14.4) |

### 2.3 Probability that it flies

Target selection will be driven by Fe-Ni yield. My judgement:
- P(selected target is C-complex and hydrated) ≈ 20–40%.
- This rises to 30–50% if a CR-like metal-plus-hydrated body is found.
- If the target is S, M or X type, **bom-0-6 closes at the target gate** with only the 0A sub-line spent.

---

## 3. Feedstock design basis

| Parameter | Design value | Range carried | Basis / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recoverable water at ≤650 °C | **4 wt%** | 2–8 wt% (floor 2%) | CM TGA dehydroxylation 400–770 °C (Garenne et al. 2014; King et al. 2015). Surface regolith may be partially dehydrated (Ryugu's 2.7 µm band is weaker than CI meteorites). This is deliberately below bulk meteorite H₂O. |
| Water released 150–250 °C | 15–30% of recoverable | — | Adsorbed and interlayer water |
| Water released 250–450 °C | 20–40% | — | Oxyhydroxides, early dehydroxylation |
| Water released 450–650 °C | 30–60% | — | Serpentine and saponite dehydroxylation |
| Carbon | 2–4 wt% | — | CI/CM organics and carbonates. A source of CO₂, CO, CH₄ and condensable organics. |
| Sulfur | 2–6 wt% | — | Sulfides and sulfates. Source of SO₂, H₂S and S₂; drives the material choice (§10). |
| Cl, N | 0.01–0.1 wt% | — | HCl, NH₃ in the condensate |
| Bulk density, crushed ≤2 mm | 1.1–1.3 t/m³ | — | Grain density about 2.4 t/m³; high porosity |
| Feed size | ≤2 mm | ≤5 mm acceptable | Set by heat penetration in a 4-hour batch |

The 0A characterisation campaign (§11) must replace these numbers with TGA-EGA data on CI, CM and CR meteorites, published Ryugu and Bennu sample data, and the scouts' in-situ hydration measurements.

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Top-level functional requirements (proposed)

| ID | Requirement |

| WP-F1 | Extract water from C-complex ore supplied by bom-0-3 at ≤2 mm, in microgravity, under vacuum, uncrewed. |
| WP-F2 | Produce water to Grade W1, and on demand Grade W2 (§4.3). |
| WP-F3 | Store 5–20 t of water (design 10 t) at 278–310 K, tolerating freeze–thaw without damage. |
| WP-F4 | Dispense water to bom-0-3, to tug cargo containers (bom-0-4) or to controlled rejection into tailings. |
| WP-F5 | Measure and downlink yield vs temperature, off-gas composition, condensate chemistry and component wear for each batch. |
| WP-F6 | Operate 30 days unattended. Make safe autonomously within 1 s of any fault (power, pressure, temperature). |
| WP-F7 | Keep solid release to ≥99.9% mass retention of handled ore (interim, D-03 ALARP). Vent non-condensables only through one designated vent, logged against the bom-0-15 budget. |
| WP-F8 | Produce no LOX, LH₂ or stored H₂/O₂ inventory. The diagnostic electrolysis cell recombines its products (§6.7). |

### 4.2 Performance requirements

| Parameter | Threshold | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| Water output (at 4 wt% ore) | 10 t/yr | 25–30 t/yr |
| Extraction efficiency (captured ÷ TGA-recoverable at the same profile) | ≥75% | ≥90% |
| Availability | ≥60% | ≥75% |
| Canister seal life | 500 thermal cycles | 1,500 |
| Specific heating energy (electric, at the retort) | ≤0.45 kWh/kg ore | ≤0.30 |

## 6. Subsystem specifications

### 6.1 Feed and canister station

- **Feed buffer:** 2 m³ hopper with an agitated screw outlet. It receives ore by enclosed conveyor from bom-0-3, which owns crushing and sizing.
- **Canisters:**
  - 14 in service plus 2 spare (spares booked in bom-0-14).
  - FeCrAl, 0.30 m³, Ø 0.70 m × 0.80 m, 38–45 kg each.
  - Internal radial fins on a 60 mm pitch improve heat penetration.
- **Lid seal:** double metal C-ring (silver-plated, sulfidation-tolerant alloy). The flange runs about 150 °C cooler than the bed because of a finned standoff. There is a leak-check port between the rings.
- **Fill:** 330 kg at about 1.15 t/m³ and 95% fill. It is centrifugally compacted at about 0.1 g during fill.
- **Handling:** a pilot-owned 2-axis gantry loader (0.25 t) moves canisters between the fill station, retort sleeves and dump chute. Nothing touches hot solids except the canister interior. Emptying runs at under 80 °C by reverse spin and lid-open into an enclosed tailings chute.

### 6.2 Canister-retorts (×2, counter-rotating)

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Configuration | Fixed resistive heater sleeve; the canister spins inside on cool-end bearings |
| Spin rate | 20–40 rpm (0.18–0.7 g at r = 0.35 m; nominal 30 rpm ≈ 0.35 g) |
| Angular momentum | The pair counter-rotates, so net angular momentum is under 5% of one unit. This avoids torque on bom-0-3 structure. |
| Heater | NiCr/FeCrAl elements outside the canister, in a sealed Ar-filled sleeve; 30 kW per retort peak |
| Bed temperature envelope | 150–800 °C qualified; profile nominally capped at 650 °C |
| Internal pressure | 0.1–5 kPa. Low pressure lowers dehydration temperature and limits retained water. |
| Sweep | Optional recirculated CO₂ or H₂O at 0.1–1 g/s to shorten residence time (an experiment variable) |
| Vapour exit | Axial port, cooled rotary joint (bellows-loaded carbon face plus labyrinth) at under 200 °C. Leakage goes outward to vacuum. |
| Mixing | Stationary plough on a retractable arm. It turns the centrifugally packed bed once per revolution. |
| Insulation | Multi-foil plus microporous silica; sleeve OD ≤1.1 m, skin ≤60 °C |
| Mass per retort | 0.65–0.75 t including drive, sleeve, insulation and joint |

**Energy check (per batch)**
- Ore: 330 kg × 0.30 kWh/kg = 99 kWh.
- Canister and fins: about 4 kWh.
- Sleeve losses at about 4 kW × 4.3 h ≈ 17 kWh.
- Total: about 120 kWh per batch, or 28 kW average per retort. Two retorts staggered draw about 56 kWₑ.
- The envelope is 0.15–0.45 kWh/kg ore. There is no heat recuperation in the pilot; at 56 kW, the hardware cost of recovery exceeds the array cost it saves (§12.4).

**Throughput check**
- 2 retorts × 5 batches/day × 330 kg = 3.3 t/day.
- At 70% availability: 843 t/yr ore.
- At 4 wt% and 90% capture: **30 t/yr**. At 2 wt%: 15 t/yr. At 75% capture and 60% availability: 10–22 t/yr.

### 6.3 Hot-gas filtration and pre-cooling

- **Filters:** sintered FeCrAl candles at about 400 °C. Area 0.4 m² per train; dual trains with back-pulse using the process gas. Removal ≥99.9% at ≥1 µm. Most dust is already rejected centrifugally because vapour leaves at the axis.
- **Pre-cooler:** finned counterflow gas-to-liquid exchanger feeding the main pumped loop (Galden, or a water/glycol loop kept above freezing). It cools gas from about 920 K to 310–320 K. Gas stays above the water dew point (about 280 K at 1 kPa H₂O), so no condensation occurs in the pre-cooler.

### 6.4 Cold traps (vapour deposition)

| Item | Trap 1A/1B (water) | Trap 2A/2B (secondary) |
|---|---|---|
| Fin temperature | 245–255 K | 185–200 K |
| Fin area | 4 m² each | 1.5 m² each |
| Frost capacity | 40 kg each (about 8 mm frost) | 5 kg each |
| Cycle | Deposit ≤8 h, then isolate, melt at 280–285 K in a sealed volume, drain under bladder pressure | Deposit ≤48 h, then regenerate into a chemisorbent bed |
| Cooling | Pumped loop to the 25 m² cold radiator | 1.5 kWₑ Stirling or pulse-tube cooler (load ≤0.5 kW, about 20% Carnot) |
| Design load | Average 3.9 kW (120 kg/day × 2.83 MJ/kg deposition). Peaks of 10–12 kW are buffered by fin and frost thermal mass. | ≤0.5 kW |

**Cold radiator sizing**
- Rejection: ε = 0.9, two-sided, at 235 K, gives σT⁴ ≈ 0.9 × 5.67×10⁻⁸ × 3.05×10⁹ ≈ 156 W/m² per side, or about 310 W/m² in total.
- Allowing for an NEA IR and albedo environment with a sunshade, net rejection is about 200–250 W/m².
- 3.9 kW average therefore needs 16–20 m². **I specify 25 m² (range 20–40).** The radiator sits behind a 30 m² single-layer shade.
- This is the only "sunshield" in the item. It is a radiator shade, not a cryogenic shield.

**Contamination logic**
- Water deposits selectively at 250 K, because CO₂'s frost point at its partial pressure is about 150 K.
- SO₂, NH₃ and heavier organics partly co-deposit. That is why stage 3 is routed separately and why Trap 2 exists.
- Non-condensables (CO₂, CO, CH₄, N₂, H₂) are vented. Estimated mass is 0.3–1.5% of ore, so 3–13 t/yr. **This is comparable to water output and must be in the bom-0-15 budget.**

### 6.5 Purification

The heritage is the ISS Water Processor Assembly architecture, whose daily throughput of about 100 kg/day is the same order as our 85–120 kg/day. The feed, however, is very different: acidic, high in sulfur, high in organics. The design accounts for that difference rather than assuming heritage carries over.

| Stage | Function | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Membrane degasser | Removes dissolved CO₂, H₂S, SO₂ | Gas returns to Trap 2 |
| Neutralising and activated-carbon bed | Raises pH, adsorbs organics | Consumable |
| Catalytic oxidation reactor (about 130 °C, O₂ from the recombiner side-stream or stored) | TOC from about 100 ppm to under 1 ppm | WPA-like VRA |
| Mixed-bed ion exchange | Conductivity from tens of µS/cm to ≤1 µS/cm | Largest consumable |
| 0.2 µm filter and UV | Particulates | — |
| Polish loop | W1 to W2 on demand | — |
| Capacity | 150 kg/day design (1.3–1.8× the average need) | — |
| Power | 2–5 kWₑ | — |
| Consumables | 150–400 kg/yr resin and carbon (resupplied via bom-0-14). Depends strongly on stage 3 contaminant load. | Key 0A measurement |

I agree with Claude that gas cleanup belongs inside bom-0-6. Gemini's separate $80–150M skid is over-scoped for 120 kg/day.

### 6.6 Storage and disposition

- **Tanks:** 2 × 5 m³ bladders, fluoropolymer-lined, aramid-restrained, inside a 0.6 t housing. Total 10 t (range 5–20 t).
- **Freeze-thaw tolerance:** verified for ≥50 cycles. Survival heating is not relied upon.
- **Fill time:** 10 t at 25 t/yr fills in about 5 months. **I reject both Claude's 100–1,000 t and GPT's 30–100 t inventories for this pilot.** A buffer larger than about six months of output only makes sense with a signed consumer.

**Disposition policy (proposed), in order:**
1. Supply bom-0-3 on request.
2. Hold a W2 reserve of at least 1 t for diagnostics and export samples.
3. Export by cargo container if a bom-0-4 trip has spare capacity and a signed requester exists.
4. Controlled rejection by injecting it into the tailings stream, where it freezes and is retained. This is never vented.

### 6.7 Diagnostic electrolysis cell

- A 1 kWₑ PEM stack processes about 3–4 kg H₂O per day at 5.6–6.5 kWh/kg. Its purpose is to prove W2 water is electrolyser-grade and to measure degradation from trace contaminants such as S and Cl.
- H₂ and O₂ are recombined catalytically and returned as water. There is no storage, no venting and no propellant.
- This is the only electrolysis in bom-0-6. Production electrolysis, if bom-0-3 adopts an H₂ loop, is bom-0-3's scope.

## 9. Autonomy, control and communications

**Light time and control approach**
- One-way light time is up to about 17 minutes at a 2 AU Earth range, plus conjunction outages of 2–4 weeks.
- Therefore all batch-level control is onboard. The ground sets campaigns: a temperature-profile matrix, sweep settings and stage routing.

**Autonomy levels (functional requirements, not labels)**

| Function | Onboard | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| Batch sequencing, stage routing, trap switching | Fully autonomous, closed-loop on RGA water signal (stage ends when dH₂O/dt < threshold) | Sets profiles |
| Purification grade control | Autonomous; diverts out-of-spec water to W0 | Approves bed changes |
| Canister handling | Autonomous with machine-vision verification | Reviews anomalies |
| FDIR | Autonomous | Post-event review |
| Experiment re-planning | Advisory onboard (suggests profiles) | Decides |

**FDIR safe-state:** heaters off, all isolation valves closed, retorts spun down over 60 s, traps held, bladders sealed, telemetry buffered for 30 days.

**Triggers:**
- Sleeve or canister over-temperature: more than 50 K above setpoint.
- Pressure more than 10 kPa, or a pressure-decay leak.
- Unexpected species, such as H₂ above 5% in the vent, which may indicate a reaction.
- Loss of power.
- Drive torque anomaly.
- Loss of the bom-0-3 interlock.

**Requirement:** 30 days unattended with ≥50% of nominal throughput maintained.

**Software:** this item reuses the bom-0-3 plant-control framework and software-classification process. It adds about 40–60k SLOC of new application code.

**Comms:** all traffic goes through bom-0-9's site relay. bom-0-6 has no direct-to-Earth link. DSN or commercial ground time is costed in bom-0-9.

## 10. Manufacturing and materials

- **Sulfidation is the main materials risk.** Ni-base superalloys suffer catastrophic sulfidation near the Ni–Ni₃S₂ eutectic (about 637 °C), which is exactly at the top of the nominal profile.
  - Canisters, fins and filters: alumina-forming FeCrAl (Kanthal APM-class), qualified for H₂S/SO₂/H₂O at 650–800 °C.
  - Heater sleeve interior: Co-Ni-Cr-Si sulfidation-resistant alloy (HR-160 class) or aluminised 310 stainless.
  - Avoid Ni-rich alloys anywhere in the hot gas path.
- **Seals:** metal C-rings with silver or gold plating checked for compatibility with sulfur. Silver tarnishes, so gold is preferred despite cost. Carbon-face rotary joint below 200 °C.
- **Wetted cold side:** 316L and Ti-6Al-4V. Assume condensate at pH 2–5 with sulfite and sulfate; the alloy choice must account for this.
- **Fabrication:**
  - FeCrAl canisters are spun or deep-drawn with electron-beam-welded fins. All 16 are a single production lot.
  - Radiators are aluminium honeycomb with embedded loop tubing, using standard spacecraft supply chains.
  - Purification is a derivative of ISS WPA ORUs from the incumbent supplier base, re-qualified for the new chemistry.
- **Production quantity:**
  - 1 flight unit.
  - 1 EDU/qualification unit, which stays on the ground as the anomaly-resolution testbed.
  - No production line. Unit cost is DDT&E-dominated.
- **Test infrastructure:** a thermal-vacuum chamber of at least 5 m with a cold shroud representative of the radiator environment. A spin rig. Sulfur-tolerant exhaust handling. A CI/CM simulant supply of about 30–60 t for EDU campaigns: commercially available CI and CM simulants, spiked to TGA-matched water, C and S content.

## 14. Disagreements with Round 2

### 14.1 Gemini: 2 units, 1,500 t/yr, $250–450M, high confidence (rejected)

**Scale does not fit the site**
- 1,500 t/yr at 4 wt% needs 37.5 kt/yr of ore. That is 5× the ore needed for about 1 kt/yr of Fe-Ni product, and above the abandoned 25 kt/yr central-station scale.
- Heating alone would be 37.5 kt × 0.3 kWh/kg ≈ 11 GWh/yr, or about 1.3 MWₜₕ continuous. That consumes most of a 1–2.5 MWₑ site.

**No Phase 0 consumer at that scale**
- There is no LOX/LH₂ and water EP is a desk study.
- Even Gemini's own fleet propellant estimate (380–510 t/yr) assumes water EP, which D-05 does not select.

**Confidence**
- High confidence is not supportable for a technology at TRL 2–4.

### 14.2 Claude: 1 × 10–100 t/yr, $150–400M (upper end rejected)

- I agree with the lower half. 100 t/yr needs 2.5–5 kt/yr of side-stream ore, which turns a pilot into a production unit without a consumer.
- The top of the cost range follows from that upper sizing.
- I agree with Claude's placement of gas cleanup and its real-options framing.

### 14.3 GPT: 1 × 10–30 t/yr, $100–300M (closest)

- I adopt GPT's quantity.
- I raise the cost floor to $135M for 0B plus $15M for 0A because of the sulfidation-qualified EDU and the purification re-qualification.
- I adopt GPT's position that heating should be counted once, but I assign pilot retort heating to bom-0-6 because the pilot owns its retorts.

### 14.4 Water EP as a sizing driver (rejected for bom-0-6)

- Propellant demand is ṁ = 2ηP/vₑ². At Isp 1,000 s and η = 0.5, that is about 330 t per MWₑ-yr.
- A fleet of 10–18 tugs at 1–2.5 MWₑ needs 3–15 kt/yr at full duty.
- That is 100–500× this pilot and about 10–50× even option W-2.
- Water EP would need its own Phase 1-scale gate. The pilot's contribution is impurity data for the desk study only.

### 14.5 Reconciliation content now superseded

- **Siting at L4/L5:** superseded; processing is co-located at the NEA.
- **The PEM production chain** (5.2–7.0 kWh/kg; 7–11 kWh/kg chain): applies only to the diagnostic cell and to bom-0-3 if it adopts an H₂ loop.
- **The cryocooler dispute** (700 W vs 1–11 kWₑ), the rq-0-30 subcooling margin, rq-0-47/48 heat leak and MLI, and the 35–60 m sunshield: all moot for Phase 0. **I recommend these deliberations be marked "Phase 1 reference, not applicable to Phase 0"** under bom-0-7 configuration control, rather than corrected and written back into a Phase 0 specification.
- **The 25 kt/yr gate:** irrelevant to this item. My gates are target, consumer and TRL (§11.2), consistent with Claude and GPT's Round 2 demand-gate logic.

### 14.6 Water inventory

- Claude's 100–1,000 t and GPT's 30–100 t are both larger than this pilot needs.
- I specify 10 t (5–20 t), plus a disposition policy (§6.6) that ends in retention in tailings, never venting.
